target.name: PreyVR native zero-g flight controls and scoped Steam acceleration basis

question: Can the supported Steam zero-g movement path accept headset-aligned native flight requests through a proved rotation/input contract with scoped cleanup in source and offline fixtures?
claim: Steam instructions prove state 9 dispatch to native ZeroG update, the complete player/FSM/input/entity receiver flow, ascent/descent signs, concrete CEntity world-rotation getter at slot +0x150 and the boost/brake input producers and consumers. The implementation limits its quaternion override to the single acceleration read and retains the original getter for every other caller. Production-adapter fixtures confirm coherent head-relative 3D steering, held-entry neutral quarantine, exact caller/entity/context gating, native-request cleanup and debt after a possible setter write, modal/ground/hacking handoff, replacement-player refusal and live cinematic gating. This confirms static/source and harness contracts, not native gameplay acceptance.
method: MSVC 19.50 x64 Release with Visual Studio 18 2026, CMake/CTest and Python 3.12 offline PE/PAK checks. Local EGS/PDB exports supplied search candidates; masked prefixes located Steam bodies, then actual Steam instructions, dispatch data, constructor/vtable, numerical constants and installed base/patch profiles established the contract. No fixed EGS-to-Steam address delta was used. Ghidra preflight found no running instance. The verifier checks actual C++ gate arrays and rejects corrupted concrete-callee and field-gate controls. Pure state/basis tests plus the actual production adapter run with explicit native/tracking/HUD boundary substitutions; the native bridge is not called on fake memory. Final Release build and 82/82 combined offline tests pass. Production World-page raster inspected. Every package/ZIP manifest file matches the tested binaries. Reproduction commands and exact source/DLL identities are frozen. No game, injection, xr-sim session, launcher run or headset test.

identity.reason: Pinned complete source commit, integration base and tested DLL/package hashes. Native verifier requires Steam PreyDll.dll SHA256 7D6E322F61B28331095A400F0BA5F09BD9A39C57BF993602285DD6ACB05311A7, x64 PE and explicit image-base/RVA conventions.

instrument.reason: Target instruction/dispatch/vtable/constant checks, corrupt callee/field negative controls and bounded PAK reader KAT/CRC validation. Adapter fixtures execute production code with named substituted boundaries; GDI raster uses the production painter. Package checker compares all directory/ZIP files and the tested DLL.

control.reason: State 9 versus gravity shaft/unknown owner; valid versus unrelated getter caller/entity and changed epoch/reference; neutral versus held entry; accepted versus refused altitude cleanup; setter failure after write with refused rollback; matching versus mismatched player pose; fresh focus versus cleared tracking; live cinematic flag versus stale analog observation. Numerical pitch/yaw and native w-first quaternion checks are independent expected outputs.

scene.reason: Static files and synthetic native-boundary/graphics fixtures, not a running Prey zero-g scene.

restore.reason: Persistent version-controlled changes and a separate new local test package. No game process, user VR preference or shared runtime configuration was changed. Older test packages were retained.

baseline.reason: Final integrated Release build, static contract verifier and 82/82 offline tests pass. Packaged and archived file hashes match. This baseline concerns source/harness health; native launch, input acceptance, rendering, comfort and performance remain unmeasured.

limits: No actual hook execution, native flight acceptance, save-transition behavior, stance/camera-height behavior, headset alignment/comfort or performance measured. Shipping profile bindings are not proof of custom user remaps. Ordinary zero-g state 9 is supported; gravity shafts and other movement states retain their existing paths. Controller-directed flight and physical surface anchoring/push-off are not implemented. Native input/physics still owns acceleration, speed limits, inertia and collision; helper return success is not proof that the next simulation accepted a request. Steering refuses stale or mismatched metadata. Local package is a development test build, not a release or headset-approved build.

next_action: Push the consolidated integration source, then test ordinary EVA/GUTS flight in the game: head/body basis, A/B ascent/descent and braking, Y boost/release, menus, recenter, tracking loss, landing, save replacement and crouched entry. Establish native/headset acceptance before adding surface grab/push-off. Candidate for scoped native-input/consumer-basis playbook review; no bottleneck clearance or runtime promotion.
